name: Full-Frame vs Retrofit Window Replacement for Older Aluminum Windows

mainEntity.name: For Los Angeles County homes with original single-pane aluminum windows, when does it make more sense to do full-frame replacement instead of retrofit installation?
mainEntity.text: For Los Angeles County homes with original single-pane aluminum windows, when does it make more sense to do full-frame replacement instead of retrofit installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many Los Angeles County tract homes still have original single-pane aluminum windows. Retrofit installations insert new frames into the existing metal frame, which is faster and less invasive but leaves the old frame in place. This can slightly reduce glass area and may not fully address thermal bridging or air leaks. Retrofit is usually acceptable when the existing frame is structurally sound, square, and free of corrosion or water damage. Full-frame replacement involves removing the entire existing window, including the old frame, down to the rough opening. This allows the installer to inspect for hidden rot, stucco cracks, or framing damage, add new flashing and insulation, and sometimes slightly adjust the opening for better sizing. Full-frame replacement is often the better choice when aluminum frames show corrosion, condensation issues, or drafts you cannot resolve with weatherstripping. If you plan a major exterior repaint or stucco repair anyway, full-frame replacement becomes more attractive because associated patching can be bundled. Ask your contractor to inspect several openings, especially on sun-exposed or weather-facing walls, and to show you photos of any damage. Compare quotes for both methods, including finish work, and consider the long-term comfort, resale value, and opportunity to increase visible glass.
acceptedAnswer.description: Full-frame window replacement makes more sense than retrofit in many Los Angeles County homes with original single-pane aluminum when frames are corroded, leaking, poorly insulated, or when you want larger glass area, better air sealing, or to address hidden water damage around the opening.
